text:
laura: hitting weird failures in prod after upgrading to python-sdk 0.12.3 — requests suddenly time out during long generations and some calls return 401 intermittently. anyone seen auth flakes + timeouts together?

sam: ugh. do you have a repro? 401 + timeout sounds like token refresh race or a proxy dropping keepalives.

laura: repro attached below. minimal script: 
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="redacted", timeout=(5, 300))  # connect 5s, read 300s
print(client.generate(model="open-llama-13b", prompt="x"))
```
But on long gen we see read timeout after ~30s even though read=300. sometimes first request returns 401 then subsequent succeed.

support-bot: New support ticket #15432 created for laura (escalation).

ryan: which python HTTP backend are you using? httpx or requests? the SDK uses httpx by default but can fall back. also which env vars for timeouts?

laura: running with httpx 0.24.3, uvicorn proxy in front, env has REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=30 (legacy envvar...). we only recently added explicit timeout=(5,300) in code.

alice: that env var is the culprit. REDWOOD_TIMEOUT is interpreted as the "total" deadline in the older config layer and will override client args if set. behavior: env var > client arg when both present. not great.

sam: confirmed — env parsing bug in 0.12.3: it converts env var to int seconds and wires it to httpx Timeout(total=env) which ends up truncating streaming read deadlines. open a patch?

laura: ok that explains read cutoff, but what about the 401s? saw one 401 for a token-auth'd private deployment after ~10 minutes of idle.

eng-runtime: 401s after idle might be short-lived access token TTL on our side + client not refreshing before request. python SDK had a race when background refresh and request happen concurrently — older versions retried refresh, but 0.12.3 introduced a non-blocking refresh path that can occasionally let a failing request through.

ryan: both issues together would definitely surface as "intermittent auth then timeout" if proxy/ALB also terminates idle keepalive earlier. what does your proxy keepalive look like?

laura: ALB idle timeout was 60s. we were seeing read timeouts ~30s because REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=30. so sequence: idle > new request triggers token refresh race -> sometimes 401 -> client retries but env total deadline already low so the retry exhausts the deadline and we get timeout.

sam: repro steps to share with eng: 1) set REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=30 2) run the long-gen script for ~2 minutes and let idle > 60s 3) observe occasional 401 then client-level ReadTimeout. include httpx logs with TRACE.

alice: workaround until patch: unset REDWOOD_TIMEOUT or set REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=0 (means disabled) and pass explicit Timeout object via code: `client = Client(timeout=httpx.Timeout(5, read=600))`. also bump ALB keepalive > app gen latency.

laura: tried unset env var — stable now for a few runs. will wait for eng patch. thanks. :tada:

eng-runtime: filed GH issue #5892 and PR drafted to 0.12.4 to: 1) make env var behavior additive (env won't override explicit client Timeout), 2) fix token refresh locking so requests block until refreshed, and 3) add more logging for retry+deadline events. linking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/12345

billing-bot: Note: some calls that timed out were double-billed due to duplicate retries recorded before idempotency dedupe. billing team alerted.

laura: flagged billing team. will share specific request ids from logs.

sam: thanks — for triage notes: root cause = legacy REDWOOD_TIMEOUT envvar overriding client timeout + token refresh race in 0.12.3, amplified by ALB idle config. Mitigations: unset env var or pin to 0, upgrade to 0.12.4 when released, increase ALB keepalive.

laura: adding final repro snippet and httpx TRACE command: 
```bash
export REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=30
export HTTPX_LOG_LEVEL=trace
python long_gen_repro.py  # same script as above
```

support-bot: Ticket #15432 updated: awaiting customer verification after workaround.

ryan: let us know if you want a temporary signed token TTL extension from infra while you upgrade.

laura: appreciate it, will reach out if needed.
